findings.claim: The education-c3 rework fixed the untaught mechanics but turned q17 and q19 into near-copies of existing bank items with one reasoning step. That breaks line 71 ('needs at least two reasoning steps') and section 6's own rule (line 169) that a same-mechanism, same-decision item must add a second reasoning step. q17 is now 'choose the code that removes matching records safely while scanning', with no secondary objective. That is the same mechanism and decision as lists bank 'removing while scanning' ('Which line removes them safely?'). The 'second step' line 173 lists for it, a new record context plus a stream distractor, is a new context and a distractor, not a reasoning step. q17 is also labelled Analyze, but it is a single choose-the-safe-call decision. q19 is now 'put, get and getOrDefault calls on a map with wrapper values; locate each boxing and unboxing'. That matches wrapper bank 'spotting unboxing' ('Which line unboxes a value?') and overlaps 'unboxing null' (map get into a primitive). Section 6 has no entry for q19 at all. Evidence: coverage map line 84 (q19), line 100 (q17), lines 169-178 (no q19 entry; q17 entry at 173); collections-streams/collections-in-depth/lists-sets-and-maps-in-depth/artifact.gift 'o2 - removing while scanning'; collections-streams/collections-in-depth/wrapper-types-and-autoboxing/artifact.gift 'o1 - spotting unboxing' and 'o2 - unboxing null'.
findings.recommendation: Give q17 and q19 a real second reasoning step that uses taught material only. For q17, for example, also decide whether the safe call works on a list made with List.of. That adds lists#o3, which line 148 says no item can carry. For q19, for example, locate the boxing and also predict a taught consequence such as a null unbox or identity versus equals. Otherwise label each one honestly as the same skill in a new context. Add q19 to section 6 as a close shape of the two wrapper bank items, and check q17's level label.

findings.claim: The reworked q30 ('choose the stream pipeline that is equivalent to a loop that filters, transforms and sorts loaded records') has two problems. (1) It is labelled Evaluate, which line 76 defines as 'choose and defend under competing needs', but picking the equivalent translation has no competing needs. It is Apply or Analyze, so the stated rising order is no longer true at the last item. (2) It matches the existing review page's own translation activity. That activity translates a pipeline that filters, maps and sorts into a loop ('test, map and add inside the loop, and sort after it'), and translates a loop into filter/groupingBy/counting. Section 6 has no close-shape entry for q30. Evidence: collections-streams/lambdas-and-streams/collections-and-streams-review/artifact.md lines 13, 37, 67; coverage map line 76 (Evaluate definition) and lines 158-180 (no q30 entry).
findings.recommendation: Either relabel q30 Analyze and move it before the Evaluate block, recounting the level totals in line 76. Or give it a real evaluate decision, for example choosing between two non-equivalent pipelines where one changes the order or drops records under a stated need. Add a section 6 entry naming the review page's translation activity, with q30's second step.

findings.claim: The new reason for leaving lists-sets-and-maps-in-depth#o3 untargeted is factually wrong. It says 'no other item keeps this objective without exceeding two objectives', but four items have no secondary objective: q17, q19, q22 and q25. q17 is on the same topic, and a List.of variant is a natural extension of its removal decision. This objective was a secondary in the previous plan, so the rework reduced coverage from 40 to 39 on a reason that does not hold. Evidence: Programmatic check of the section 4 table: secondary is '-' for q17, q19, q22 and q25.
findings.recommendation: Make lists#o3 q17's secondary, which also supplies q17's second reasoning step (see education-d1), and update the blueprint objectives, objectiveFormats and the counts. Otherwise give a reason that is true.

findings.claim: The count rationale says the 9 secondary-only objectives are 'spread over 8 topics'. They span 9 distinct topics: big-o, choosing, generics, how-hashmap, stacks, equals, grouping, lambdas and streams-db. So the 39-item alternative would weight 9 of 15 topics 3:2, not 8. Evidence: Programmatic: set(secondaries) minus set(primaries) = 9 objectives in 9 distinct topics.
findings.recommendation: Correct the count to 9 topics, or recount after any education-d3 change.
